title: Farah Khan's Triplets Head to Three Different US Universities in Emotional Family Milestone
excerpt: Filmmaker Farah Khan bids farewell as Diva, Anya, and Czar move to Babson, NYU, and Emory to pursue entrepreneurship, economics, and AI.
body:
• Filmmaker Farah Khan and Shirish Kunder's triplets — Diva, Anya, and Czar — have moved to three different US cities for college.
  • Diva will study Entrepreneurship and Finance at Babson College, Anya will pursue Economics and Data Science at NYU, and Czar chose Artificial Intelligence of Business at Emory University.
  • The 17-year-olds graduated from Dhirubhai Ambani International School (DAIS) in Mumbai earlier this year.
  • Farah shared an emotional Instagram post about the "3 cities, 3 campuses, 3 goodbyes" experience.

Filmmaker and choreographer Farah Khan and her husband, editor Shirish Kunder, are navigating a milestone familiar to Indian parents worldwide: sending their children to college in the United States. The twist — they had to do it three times over, in three different cities, for their triplets Diva, Anya, and Czar.

Three Kids, Three Campuses, Three Goodbyes

Farah shared the bittersweet occasion on Instagram on September 6, posting a series of photographs from the send-offs. "If u thought moving ur kid to college was hard.. try doing it 3times! 3 cities, 3 campuses..3 goodbyes! 3pieces of my heart," she wrote, adding, "Jao jee lo apni zindagi.. but remember, all roads lead back to Dad & mom."

https://x.com/dna/status/2096610449014018551

The first image showed Farah hugging her son Czar, while other photos captured candid moments with all three children. She set the post to the song "Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna." Her husband Shirish, she noted, handled "everything except cming in the family pics."

"If u thought moving ur kid to college was hard.. try doing it 3times! 3 cities, 3 campuses..3 goodbyes! 3pieces of my heart."

— Farah Khan, on Instagram

Where They're Headed

Each of the triplets, born in 2008 and now 17, has chosen a distinct academic path at a different US institution. Diva will study Entrepreneurship and Finance at Babson College, which has campuses in Wellesley, Boston, and Miami and is consistently ranked among the top schools for entrepreneurship. Anya is headed to New York University to pursue Economics and Data Science. Czar will study Artificial Intelligence of Business at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

All three graduated from Dhirubhai Ambani International School (DAIS) in Mumbai. Their college acceptances were shared on the DAIS Class of 2026 Instagram page, prompting Farah to celebrate what she called a "#hattrick."

Bollywood Reacts

The post drew emotional responses from industry colleagues. Sunita Kapoor commented, "Faru making me cry." Shilpa Shirodkar wrote, "Trust me they will come back being the Best Version of Themselves." Rhea Kapoor added, "I can't believe they are so big." Bhavana Pandey, Soha Ali Khan, and Diana Penty also responded with heart emojis.

Fans on social media remarked on how quickly time had passed. "I still remember when she had triplets and when they were babies," one wrote. Others recalled Farah's pregnancy during the filming of "Om Shanti Om" in 2007. The couple married in 2004 and welcomed their triplets in 2008.

A Relatable Journey for NRI Families

Farah's experience echoes a transition thousands of Indian families navigate every fall — the logistics, emotions, and adjustments of sending children to American universities. The added complexity of simultaneous departures to three different cities adds a layer most parents won't face, but the underlying sentiment — pride mixed with the ache of an emptying home — is universal for diaspora families on both sides of the move.
